tagline: Over the Blue Ridge at Rockfish Gap, then down its valley.
intro: Out of Charlottesville, US 250 runs west as Ivy Road over the Mechums River, roughly on the line of the colonial Three Notch'd Road, named, it is believed, for the three notches cut in trees to blaze it. Past the Route 151 junction it climbs the Blue Ridge as the Rockfish Gap Turnpike.

A mile short of the gap Route 6 turns off and comes down Afton Mountain in curves through the village of Afton, follows the Rockfish Valley and then the Rockfish River, and crosses into Albemarle through a gap between Shiloh and Butler mountains. The ground gentles on the way to Scottsville.

moments.title: Rockfish Gap
moments.text: At about 1,900 feet the turnpike tops the Blue Ridge in a gap the Appalachian Trail also uses, a short way from where Skyline Drive meets the Blue Ridge Parkway.

moments.title: Faber
moments.text: A Nelson County community where Route 6 crosses the railroad, named in several episodes of The Waltons, which drew on the lay of this country.

moments.title: Esmont
moments.text: A farming town on old plantation land whose quarries made it the nation's largest soapstone producer by the mid-1920s, with a depot and three stores at its peak.
